In [[differential geometry]] in mathematics, the '''Vafa–Witten equations''' are the gauge [[Field equation|field equations]] of '''Vafa–Witten theory''', which is obtained as a [[topologically]] twisted [[N = 4 supersymmetric Yang-Mills theory]] (TT N = 4 SYM) using the '''Vafa–Witten twist'''. The Vafa–Witten equations are formulated on four-dimensional [[Smooth manifold|manifolds]] (short [[4-manifold]]s), representing [[spacetime]] in physics, and as [[Partial differential equation|partial differential equations]] depend on its [[smooth structure]]. Considering the [[moduli space]] of its solutions, which are all solutions up to [[Gauge group (mathematics)|gauge]], meaning physical equivalence, therefore encodes informations about it, similar to the much more well-known [[Yang–Mills moduli space]] and [[Seiberg–Witten moduli space]]. The Vafa–Witten equations are named after [[Cumrun Vafa]] and [[Edward Witten]].

== Topological twist ==
A topological twist is a choice for how the four-dimensional [[spin group]] <math>\operatorname{Spin}(4)=\operatorname{SU}(2)\times\operatorname{SU}(2)</math> acts on the canonical inclusion [[Representation theory|representation]] <math>\mathbf{4}\colon\operatorname{SU}(4)\hookrightarrow\operatorname{GL}_4(\mathbb{C})</math> of the [[R-symmetry]] group, which relates the [[topology]] to the [[supersymmetry]]. The Vafa–Witten twist is then the splitting <math>(\mathbf{1},\mathbf{2})\oplus(\mathbf{1},\mathbf{2})</math>.<ref name=":0">Manshot 23, p. 11-14</ref>

== Development ==

In 1988, Edward Witten developed [[topological quantum field theory]] (TQFT),<ref>{{Cite journal |last=Witten |first=Edward |title=Topological quantum field theory |journal=Communications in Mathematical Physics |date=1988 |volume=117 |issue=3 |pages=353–386 |bibcode=1988CMaPh.117..353W |doi=10.1007/BF01223371 |mr=0953828 |s2cid=43230714}}</ref> a contribution listed for his [[Fields Medal]] in 1990,<ref>{{Cite web |title=Fields Medals 1990 - Breakthroughs in Mathematics and Physics |url=https://www.mathunion.org/imu-awards/fields-medal/fields-medals-1990 |access-date=2026-07-04 |website=www.mathunion.org}}</ref> and used it to showed that [[Donaldson theory]], a contribution listed for [[Simon Donaldson]]'s Fields Medal in 1986,<ref name=":3">{{Cite web |title=Fields Medals 1986 - Donaldson, Faltings, Freedman Achievements |url=https://www.mathunion.org/imu-awards/fields-medal/fields-medals-1986 |access-date=2026-07-04 |website=www.mathunion.org}}</ref> is a TT [[N = 2 supersymmetric Yang-Mills theory|N = 2 SYM]]. In 1994, [[Nathan Seiberg]] and Edward Witten then constructed the dual TT N = 2 SYM, known as [[Seiberg–Witten theory]].<ref>{{Cite journal |last1=Seiberg |first1=Nathan |author-link1=Nathan Seiberg |last2=Witten |first2=Edward |author-link2=Edward Witten |title=Electric-Magnetic Duality, Monopole Condensation, and Confinement in N = 2 Supersymmetric Yang-Mills Theory |journal=[[Nuclear Physics B]] |date=1994 |volume=426 |issue=1 |pages=19–52 |arxiv=hep-th/9407087 |doi=10.1016/0550-3213(94)90124-4 |bibcode=1994NuPhB.426...19S }}</ref><ref>{{Cite journal |last1=Seiberg |first1=Nathan |author-link1=Nathan Seiberg |last2=Witten |first2=Edward |author-link2=Edward Witten |date=1994 |title=Monopoles, Duality and Chiral Symmetry Breaking in N = 2 Supersymmetric QCD |journal=[[Nuclear Physics B]] |volume=431 |issue=3 |pages=484–550 |arxiv=hep-th/9408099 |doi=10.1016/0550-3213(94)90214-3 |bibcode=1994NuPhB.431..484S }}</ref> Both theories were very successful in describing smooth 4-manifolds. Later development then shifted from the N = 2 case with two inequivalent twists to the N = 4 case with three inequivalent twists. Besides the [[Vafa–Witten twist]], these are the [[Donaldson–Witten twist]] (<math>(\mathbf{1},\mathbf{2})\oplus(\mathbf{1},\mathbf{1})\oplus(\mathbf{1},\mathbf{1})</math>) and the [[Kapustin–Witten twist]] (<math>(\mathbf{2},\mathbf{1})\oplus(\mathbf{1},\mathbf{2})</math>).<ref name=":0" />

== Field equations ==
The [[Boson|bosonic]] fields of Vafa–Witten theory are a [[gauge field]] <math>A</math> with [[field strength]] <math>F</math>, a [[scalar field]] <math>\Phi</math> and a [[self-dual 2-form]] <math>B</math>. The Vafa–Witten equations are then given by:<ref name=":0" />
:<math>F_{\mu\nu}^++\frac{1}{2}[C,B_{\mu\nu}^+]+\frac{1}{4}[B_{\mu\kappa}^+,B_{\nu\lambda}^+]g^{\kappa\lambda}=0;</math>
:<math>D_\mu C+D^\nu B_{\mu\nu}^+=0.</math>
